messages:
maria (oncall): FYI seeing a big spike in queued requests and 503s from eu-west over the last ~15m. Latency SLO violations and some customers complaining.
ops-bot: ALERT: region-eu-west queue-depth > 95th pct threshold (5m) — rolling 5m avg 182 -> action: page oncall.
jon (sre): I'm on it. Do we have any recent deploys or routing changes?
maria (oncall): No deploys this hour. Console shows sudden fallback traffic to dedicated pools around 14:03 UTC.
tara (infra): Confirmed — an automated regional failover pushed traffic to dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-a and they hit admission limits quickly. Pool metrics show sustained GPU UTIL > 99% and long runqueue.
kev (runtime): Dedicated pool admission controller is supposed to cap inflight at 1200 tokens but the rate-limiter was returning 0 for a short window due to a token-replenish bug. When the fallback kicked in, the admission check returned "allowed" incorrectly and we overcommitted.
jon (sre): Can you paste the admission logs?
kev (runtime): Pasting snippet from log around 14:03:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:58Z admission: CheckPool(pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-a) -> available=0
2026-03-18T14:03:01Z admission: AllowRequest(pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-a) -> true  # <-- incorrect
2026-03-18T14:03:01Z runtime: SpawnWorker -> OOM wait
2026-03-18T14:03:05Z queue: enqueue req=abcd latency=1200ms
```
jon (sre): That "AllowRequest -> true" when available=0 looks like the bug. Were there any config rollouts touching token math?
tara (infra): No config rollouts. But autoscaler did attempt two rapid scale-ups that returned failures due to quota limits, then scaled back down (thrash).
alex (product): Impact? Which customers and what percentage of requests?
maria (oncall): About 18% of total hosted API requests that hit eu-west were affected, ~3k rps saw elevated tail latency and ~400 5xxs over 20m. Some Dedicated customers experienced slow starts.
jon (sre): Root cause draft: regional failover pushed volume to dedicated pool; admission controller had a replenish bug under stress causing allowance to be misreported; autoscaler quota faults + rapid scale attempts caused resource churn; end result: queueing and cascading 5xxs.
kev (runtime): Additional contributing factor: prefix/KV cache had a high miss rate after failover (cold caches) increasing GPU work per request, so effective capacity dropped.
maria (oncall): Mitigation timeline: 14:03 detect -> 14:06 rollback region routing to distribute load -> 14:08 manually paused fallbacks to dedicated pools -> 14:12 forced token-restart on admission controller -> 14:18 queue drained, errors fell back to baseline.
jon (sre): Follow-ups I propose: 1) Fix token-replenish logic + add unit tests for zero-availability corner case. 2) Add a fast fail path in fallback routing if target pool reports sustained available==0 for >5s. 3) Prevent autoscaler thrash: add cooldown and backoff for quota-fail responses. 4) Add synthetic traffic test for cross-region failover scenarios.
tara (infra): Also suggest we tune cache-warmup: keep a small steady-state warm-up traffic to caches on failover for first 60s.
alex (product): We'll need a customer comms draft for anyone impacted — can ops supply a concise blurb?
maria (oncall): I'll post an incident summary in status page. Draft: "We experienced degraded performance for eu-west due to a regional failover that temporarily overloaded dedicated GPU pools. The team implemented mitigations and a permanent fix is planned." Thoughts?
\onops: (reaction) :thumbsup:
kev (runtime): Action items assigned: kev -> PR for replenish fix + tests (ETA 2d). tara -> autoscaler cooldown + quota handling (ETA 3d). jon -> rollout monitor for admission mismatches (ETA 1d). maria -> customer comms + postmortem doc (ETA EOD).
jon (sre): One more immediate step — add a fast circuit in the control plane that pauses fallback routing if aggregate pool capacity < 10% across candidate pools. I'll file a ticket.
maria (oncall): Thanks everyone. Saving logs and traces to the incident channel and attaching to the postmortem doc.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: admission-fix-branch -> staging (manual trigger required).
jon (sre): Good catch on the cache coldness. Let's include a short runbook for engineers to follow in the event of a cross-region failover.
maria (oncall): Closing monitoring alert for now. Reopening if we see any regressions. :white_check_mark:"
